To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the data from the CLSI tier 2 studies were log normally distributed for MICs and normally distributed for zone diameters; (ii) the data from these studies were used to develop statistical methods for the calculation of QC ranges that were based on the distribution of the data; (iii) these statistical methods were used to calculate QC ranges for all antimicrobial agents and QC strains for dilution testing, and for most antimicrobial agents and most QC strains for disk diffusion testing; and

(i) the statistical analysis of QC tier data sets is straightforward and can be carried out using a standard spreadsheet program, and the results are useful for the setting of QC range limits; (ii) the statistical analysis can identify possible outlier laboratories; (iii) the statistical analysis does not require a computer program; (iv) the statistical analysis is not dependent on the use of the CLSI M100 reference tables; and (v) the statistical analysis should be used to supplement the CLSI methods for
the statistical analysis of tier 2 studies for QC range setting can be performed on spreadsheets using the statistical techniques described in this paper.
